content:
The image shows:
- A soybean field in the background where plants are fully matured — brown, dried stems and pods throughout
- In the foreground, several plants with distinctly **green stems and green leaves**, clearly standing out against the fully brown/mature surrounding crop
- The green plants appear moist and vegetative while neighboring plants are at or past harvest maturity

This is the hallmark presentation of **Green Stem Disorder**: plants (or parts of plants) remain green and retain leaves while surrounding plants have senesced. The pods and seeds in the field have clearly ripened and turned brown, yet these stems remain green — exactly matching the symptom description: *"stems remain moist while pods and seeds have ripened...green stems when neighboring plants are near harvest maturity."*
